description:
The cross-surface mutation-sensitivity suite measures whether each enforced
gate's comparator actually catches a planted divergence. Two coupled defects make
it test a DIFFERENT dataset than CI gates, and leave one enforced gate uncovered:

1. Wrong scale. _build_gate_cell (tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_
   sensitivity.py:269) builds every cell with the GLOBAL EQUIVALENCE_SCALE,
   ignoring the gate's own scale_factor. H2O-DB explicitly carries
   scale_factor=_H2ODB_SCALE because its generator base is the 10M-row small tier
   - the global 0.1 would emit ~1M rows (cross_surface.py:973 comment). So the
   mutation harness measures sensitivity on a dataset that does not match the
   enforced gate, and cannot host H2O-DB at all as written.

2. Missing target. _TARGETS (test:100) lists ssb/amplab/coffeeshop/clickbench/
   joinorder_synthetic but OMITS h2odb, even though h2odb is enforced in GATES
   (cross_surface.py:973). The drift guard test_targets_cover_every_enforced_gate
   (test:332) already asserts set(_TARGETS) == set(GATES) - so it is (or should
   be) RED for h2odb. The work is to make that EXISTING guard pass and ensure its
   lane runs in CI, not to add a new guard.

anti_patterns.dont: pick an h2odb target that is vacuous (empty/all-NULL) at _H2ODB_SCALE
anti_patterns.why: the sensitivity result would be meaningless (a BS3-vacuous pass).
rely on the dataclass default; the `or` form silently substitutes policy and defeats the contract.

preserves.behavior: Existing gate mutation cells stay non-vacuous and their planted-mutation catches are unchanged.
No change to production gate behavior or to CrossSurfaceGate semantics - this is test-harness fidelity only (plus possibly a CI lane wiring).

prior_art.concept: {'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:973', 'note': 'h2odb gate definition with scale_factor=_H2ODB_SCALE and the ~100k-row bounded-cell rationale - pick an h2odb target query that is non-vacuous at that scale.'}

{'ref': 'tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py:100', 'note': '_TARGETS map and the per-target caveat comments - add h2odb with a discriminating GROUP BY + ORDER BY query returning multiple non-NULL rows.'}

{'ref': 'tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py:269', 'note': '_build_gate_cell uses gate.build(EQUIVALENCE_SCALE, ...). Change to gate.build(gate.scale_factor, ...) - scale_factor is part of the gate contract (CrossSurfaceGate dataclass default), so use it directly, NOT `gate.scale_factor or EQUIVALENCE_SCALE` (that re-leaks policy into the test).'}

{'ref': 'tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py:332', 'note': 'test_targets_cover_every_enforced_gate already asserts set(_TARGETS)==set(GATES). This item makes it pass; do not add a duplicate guard.'}

verifications.description: Every enforced gate is mutation-covered at its own scale
verifications.expected: test_targets_cover_every_enforced_gate passes (6 gates incl h2odb); all mutation kinds caught; unmutated targets green

work_units.notes:
Change _build_gate_cell to call gate.build(gate.scale_factor, tmp_path) so the
mutation cell matches the enforced-gate cell. Use the dataclass default as the
single source of truth; do not re-implement an `or EQUIVALENCE_SCALE` fallback.
Re-verify the existing parametrized gates still build non-vacuous reference
rows at their own scale.
work_units.summary: Build each mutation cell at the gate's own scale_factor

work_units.notes:
Pick an h2odb query (GROUP BY + ORDER BY) that returns multiple non-NULL rows
at _H2ODB_SCALE (~100k rows), add it to _TARGETS, and confirm
test_targets_cover_every_enforced_gate (test:332) and
test_unmutated_target_is_green pass for h2odb. The unmutated cell must be
non-empty and discriminating; each mutation kind (flip_comparator,
drop_group_key, reverse_sort, drop_join) must be CAUGHT (and reverse_sort's
documented order-blind miss for non-ORDER-BY shapes still holds where it
legitimately should).
work_units.summary: Add a non-vacuous H2O-DB mutation target and make the drift guard green

work_units.notes:
The drift guard only protects if its lane executes. Confirm the integration
lane that collects test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py runs in
.github/workflows (or add it to the appropriate required job). If it is a
slow/integration marker excluded from the default lane, ensure at least the
lightweight set(_TARGETS)==set(GATES) guard runs in a required lane so a future
gate promotion cannot silently skip mutation coverage.
work_units.summary: Confirm the mutation-sensitivity lane actually runs in CI
